title: India's I4C warns WhatsApp Web sessions left logged in on shared computers can be misused
date_note: Date of the PTI report on Telangana Today; GBHackers says the advisory was issued on 18 November, which Telangana Today does not state.
geo_basis: country of the issuing agency, capital city used
summary: India's Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre (I4C), through its National Cybercrime Threat Analytics Unit, warns that a signed-in WhatsApp Web session on a shared or public computer can be misused. Telangana Today (PTI) quotes the advisory: closing a browser window or tab does not end an authenticated session, so users must log out manually. GBHackers says the advisory names no specific exploit.
plain: India's cybercrime unit warns that closing a WhatsApp Web tab does not log you out, so someone using the same shared computer could misuse your account. It says to log out manually.
exec: India's I4C advises against official or sensitive work on WhatsApp Web, especially on shared or office computers.
action: I4C advises logging out of WhatsApp Web manually after each session, avoiding cyber cafes and public kiosks, and checking Linked Devices on the phone for unfamiliar devices.

validation.note: Telangana Today (PTI) and GBHackers independently report the I4C advisory. I4C's own page was not read; moneycontrol and livemint did not load.
